record.original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?

evidence.quote: Another open problem in RMT is to prove universality, in the bulk and at (all) the edges, for Wigner ensembles in the case that the equilibrium measure for the ensemble is supported on more than one interval. Furthermore, one would like to analyze and control situations where parameters in the underlying matrix distributions vary, and intervals in the support of the equilibrium distribution for the ensemble open and close.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $W_N$ be a sequence of $N\times N$ random Hermitian (or real symmetric) Wigner-type matrices, i.e. matrices with independent entries (up to the symmetry constraint) whose variances $s_{ij}=\mathbb{E}|W_{ij}|^2$ may depend on $i,j$ in such a way that the empirical spectral distribution of $W_N$ converges, as $N\to\infty$, to a deterministic equilibrium measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ whose support consists of more than one interval.

(a) Prove that the local eigenvalue statistics of $W_N$ are universal in the bulk of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$: for any energy $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ where $\mu$ has positive density, the rescaled $k$-point correlation functions of the eigenvalues converge to the sine-kernel determinantal (resp. Pfaffian) statistics of the GUE (resp. GOE).

(b) Prove edge universality at every spectral edge of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$, including the internal edges bordering the gaps: at each such edge the rescaled extremal eigenvalue statistics converge to the Tracy–Widom distribution of the appropriate symmetry class.

(c) Consider one-parameter families $\{W_N(t)\}_{t}$ of Wigner-type ensembles whose equilibrium measures $\mu_t$ undergo topological transitions in which two adjacent intervals of the support merge (a gap closes) or a single interval splits (a gap opens). Analyze the local eigenvalue statistics in a neighborhood of the merging point through the transition, and identify the limiting universal local statistics that interpolate between sine-kernel, Tracy–Widom edge, and the cusp (Pearcey) statistics arising at the moment of merging.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been substantially solved for Wigner-type matrices. Ajanki–Erdős–Krüger established bulk universality for general Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval support; Alt–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder and Cipolloni–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder proved edge universality at all (including internal) edges and cusp universality, completing the Wigner–Dyson–Mehta conjecture in all spectral regimes. The cusp/Pearcey statistics arise precisely at band-merging transitions, addressing the parameter-dependent opening/closing of intervals. The result has been further extended to correlated random matrices (Erdős and collaborators, 2024–2025).

status_evidence.title: Universality for general Wigner-type matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Bulk universality for general Wigner-type matrices whose density of states may be supported on multiple intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Bulk universality is established for Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval support.

status_evidence.title: Cusp Universality for Random Matrices I
status_evidence.snippet: Local eigenvalue statistics at any cusp singularity are universal; completes Wigner-Dyson-Mehta in all spectral regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Cusp universality at band-merging points is proved, handling the opening/closing of gaps.

status_evidence.title: Cusp Universality for Correlated Random Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Cusp singularities and Pearcey statistics arise in one-parameter families of Wigner-type ensembles whenever two spectral bands merge.
status_evidence.claim: The transitional regime where intervals open/close is analyzed and yields Pearcey statistics.
